interactables.name: Vivienne Vale
interactables.text: The Movie Star, [Vivienne Vale], is draped across the chaise in couture far too glamorous for grief - though she is wearing it AS grief. She points at you with a tissue. 'You. You have KIND eyes. Not like the rest of these vultures.'

topics.text: 'He was HERE, darling. I heard him at [8:00 PM], on the dot - I was mid-affirmation.' She dabs one eye, careful of the mascara. 'I would know that screech anywhere. It said: Vivienne. I am ALIVE. And possibly: garbage slop.'

topics.prompt: Paw gently at the empty cage
topics.text: 'Do NOT touch the crime scene, darling.' She sweeps you up and holds you like a press photo. 'Rudebeak is family. Rude, loud family with a [vocabulary problem] - which is the maid's doing, by the way. Rosa taught him THAT phrase. I keep a list.'

topics.prompt: Bat the little speaker out where she can see it
topics.text: She stares at it for a long moment. Something sharpens behind the movie-star eyes. 'That is not mine. That is not RUDEBEAK'S.' Then, quieter: 'This house is full of other people's equipment, darling. The [film people] wire everything. The staff hold keys to everything. Even Derek has been buying gadgets. There are cables in my walls I have never been introduced to.'

interactables.name: Petra
interactables.altText: [Petra] has moved to the window, scanning the garden the way handlers scan a horizon. 'You worked out the cage, didn't you. I can tell - you have that whisker set.' She nods once, professional to professional. 'Keep going. He is out there being inconvenient to somebody.'
interactables.text: The Bird Handler, [Petra], stands perfectly still beside an untouched bowl of seed, the way professionals wait. She gives you a nod, one working animal expert to another.

topics.text: 'His [six o'clock snack]. [He never misses it]. Never.' Her voice is flat and certain, a metronome of worry. 'Whatever happened, by six o'clock he was already somewhere he could not smell this bowl.'

topics.prompt: Tilt your head at her, professionally
topics.text: 'You want the profile? Blue-and-gold macaw, nineteen years old, ego like a rockstar, lungs like a fire alarm.' She almost smiles. 'Vain, too. Never misses his evening splash in the garden bird bath. You could set a clock by that bird's grooming.'

topics.prompt: Report the garden feathers with a slow blink
topics.text: You aim a long, deliberate blink toward the garden. She reads you perfectly. 'The bird bath. Of course - he loves that thing.' Her jaw sets. 'Understand something, cat. [Wet feathers mean a happy bird]. A happy bird does not fly away from his own bath. Someone picked him up. He only allows that when he is soggy and smug.'

keywords.displayText: Wet feathers mean a happy bird

topics.prompt: Describe the big black cases, tail twitching
topics.text: You sketch the shape of them in the air with your tail. Her face goes very still. 'Acoustic cases. The padded kind.' A long silence. 'Put him somewhere [dark and padded] and he goes quiet as a stone. He would not even cry out. Whoever picked those cases knew birds - or knew sound.'

interactables.text: The [Empty Cage]. The latch is [snapped clean off]. The seed tray is bone dry, and the feathers under the cage have [settled flat].

A thin [cable] slips out from behind the couch and vanishes into the wainscoting. You wedge into the shadow beneath the cushions: a [tiny speaker], taped to the couch frame where only somebody at whisker height would ever look.
Half under the cage stand: a single [canvas glove], smelling of mulch and outdoors. It has no business on a parquet floor.
A [lemon-oil cloth] hangs neatly over the cage stand rail. The brass gleams. Somebody polishes this cage every day - standing close enough to reach right in.
A film crew camera on a tripod, red light on. You line up behind the lens: it frames the [chaise] perfectly - Vivienne's interview spot. The cage sits [just out of frame].
A booklet: 'Phrases We've Taught Rudebeak.' Entries include: 'Hello gorgeous', 'Oscar worthy', and '[Garbage slop]' - the last one furiously crossed out and labeled: '[Maid's fault]'.

localDeductionSentence: By the time of the [early sign] the cage already stood empty - no matter what the whole house swears it heard at the [late sign]. The [way out] let the bird leave. The [trick] kept him 'home'.
